rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-sulāla derives from sallaltu al-shayʾ, extracting one thing from another.
rows.anchor: السلالة: فعالة من سللت الشيء من الشيء إذا استخرجته منه

rows.speaker: أمية
rows.claim: Umayya's verse describes creation as made from a foul extract and says all return to it, illustrating the word's sense.
rows.anchor: وقال أمية: خلق البرية من سلالة منتن ... وإلى السلالة كلها ستعود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A child is called his father's extract, as if drawn from the father's back.
rows.anchor: والولد سلالة أبيه كأنه انسل من ظهر أبيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed poet uses sūlāla for offspring, a fierce lion cub born from an unchaste progenitor.
rows.anchor: فجاءت به عصب الأديم غضنفرا ... سلالة فرج كان غير حصين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pattern conveys smallness, as do qalāma and nuḥāta.
rows.anchor: وهو بناء يدل على القلة كالقلامة والنحاتة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sīnāʾ and Sīnūn are names for a place.
rows.anchor: سيناء وسينون: اسمان لبقعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most Arabs pronounce Sīnāʾ with an open sīn; its final alif marks feminine gender, so it is diptote like ṣaḥrāʾ.
rows.anchor: وجمهور العرب على فتح سين سيناء فالألف فيه للتأنيث كصحراء

rows.speaker: الكوفيون
rows.claim: The Kufans explain Kināna's kasra pronunciation and diptote form by treating the alif of faʿlāʾ as feminine.
rows.anchor: عند الكوفيين لأنهم يثبتون أن همزة فعلاء تكون للتأنيث

rows.speaker: البصريون
rows.claim: The Basrans deny that faʿlāʾ alif marks femininity, and explain the diptote form by properness with foreignness or femininity.
rows.anchor: وعند البصريين يمتنع من الصرف للعلمية والعجمة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view identifies the place as a mountain in Palestine.
rows.anchor: كعلباء ودرحاء. قيل: وهو جبل فلسطين.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Arabic, nūr is light perceived by sight.
rows.anchor: النور في كلام العرب الضوء المدرك بالبصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ascribing light to God is figurative; one explanation takes it as the active participle, meaning He illuminates the heavens and earth.
rows.anchor: فإسناده إلى الله تعالى مجاز كما تقول:

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب وأبو جعفر
rows.claim: Ali, Abu Jaʿfar and the other listed readers read nūr as a past-tense verb and al-arḍ in the accusative, meaning God illuminated them.
rows.anchor: قراءة علي بن أبي طالب وأبي جعفر وعبد العزيز المكي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another derivation supplies a deleted dhū, giving the sense possessor of light; the following phrase supports it.
rows.anchor: وإما على حذف أي ذو نور، ويؤيده قوله مثل نوره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nūr may be praise, as Arabs call someone the sun, light, or moon of the land or tribes; the cited poetry illustrates this honorific usage.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يجعل نورا على سبيل المدح، كما قالوا فلان شمس البلاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poetry compares someone to the sun among stars and calls Khālid b. Zayd the tribes' moon; another line calls ʿAbd Allāh the moon and beauty of Marw, also transmitted with nūr.
rows.anchor: قال الشاعر: كأنك شمس والملوك كواكب وقال:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adding the heavens and earth signals the breadth and spread of God's illumination until it lights them.
rows.anchor: وأضاف النور إلى السماوات والأرض لدلالة على سعة إشراقه وفشو إضاءته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the phrase means the inhabitants of heaven and earth, who are illuminated by Him.
rows.anchor: أو يراد أهل السموات والأرض وأنهم يستضيئون به

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains the light of the heavens as the guide of their inhabitants.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: نور السماوات أي هادي أهل السموات

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid says God manages the affairs of the heavens.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: مدبر أمور السموات

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan glosses the phrase as the One who illuminates the heavens.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: منور السموات

rows.speaker: أبي
rows.claim: Ubayy explains it as God being the light of the heavens, or their light coming from Him.
rows.anchor: وقال أبي: الله به نور السموات أو منه نور السموات

rows.speaker: أبو العالية
rows.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya says God adorns heaven with sun, moon, and stars, and earth with prophets and scholars.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو العالية: مزين السموات بالشمس والقمر والنجوم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An unnamed gloss connects nūr with being free of every flaw, like a woman called Nawār who is innocent of suspicion and indecency.
rows.anchor: وقيل: المنزه من كل عيب امرأة نوار بريئة من الريبة والفحشاء

rows.speaker: الكرماني
rows.claim: Al-Kirmānī says God is seen and is the means by which creatures are seen, since He created and brought them into existence; the description is figurative.
rows.anchor: وقال الكرماني: هو الذي يرى ويرى به مجاز وصف الله به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent antecedent of the pronoun in mathalu nūrihi is God.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن الضمير في مثل نوره عائد على الله تعالى

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view takes the light as the clear signs sent down to the audience.
rows.anchor: فقيل: الآيات البينات في قوله ولقد أنزلنا إليكم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view identifies the light as faith placed in believers' hearts.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الإيمان المقذوف في قلوب المؤمنين

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view identifies the light as God's Messenger.
rows.anchor: وقيل: النور هنا هو رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says the light here is the believer.
rows.anchor: وقيل: النور هنا المؤمن. وقال

rows.speaker: كعب وابن جبير
rows.claim: Kaʿb and Ibn Jubayr take the pronoun in li-nūrihi to mean Muḥammad, making the phrase the likeness of Muḥammad's light.
rows.anchor: وقال كعب وابن جبير: الضمير في لنوره عائد على محمد

rows.speaker: أبي
rows.claim: Ubayy's reading makes the phrase the likeness of the believer's light.
rows.anchor: وقال أبي: هو عائد على المؤمنين وفي قراءته مثل نور المؤمن

rows.speaker: أبي
rows.claim: A further transmitted reading attributed to Ubayy says the likeness of one who believes in Him.
rows.anchor: وروي أيضا فيها مثل نور من آمن به

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan takes the light as the Qurʾān and faith.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: يعود على القرآن والإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The three readings that return the pronoun to Muḥammad, the believer, or Qurʾān and faith use an antecedent not explicitly mentioned; Makkī says to pause at al-arḍ on these readings.
rows.anchor: وهذه الأقوال الثلاثة عاد فيها الضمير على غير مذكور،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One analysis treats the comparison as one whole image compared with another, with no matching of individual parts.
rows.anchor: واختلفوا في هذا التشبيه أهو تشبيه جملة بجملة لا يقصد فيها إلى تشبيه جزء بجزء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the whole-image reading, God's guidance, ordered creation, and clear proofs collectively resemble the most luminous familiar image, conveying clarity to human beings.
rows.anchor: أي مثل نور الله في الوضوح كهذا الذي هو منتهاكم أيها البشر

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A detailed reading maps each part of the image to another element in the referent.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو من التشبيه المفصل المقابل جزءا بجزء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the Messenger reading, the niche is the Messenger or his chest, the lamp his prophethood and guidance, the glass his heart, the tree revelation and its angelic messengers, and the oil its proofs.
rows.anchor: فالمشكاة هو الرسول أو صدره والمصباح هو النبوة وما يتصل بها من علمه وهداه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the believer reading, the niche is the chest, the lamp faith and knowledge, the glass the heart, the tree the Qurʾān, and its oil the proofs and wisdom it contains.
rows.anchor: وعلى قول المؤمن فالمشكاة صدره والمصباح الأيمان والعلم.

rows.speaker: أبي
rows.claim: Ubayy says the believer in this best state moves among people like a living person walking among the dead in graves.
rows.anchor: قال أبي: فهو على أحسن الحال يمشي في الناس كالرجل الحي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the Qurʾān-and-faith reading, the image is faith and Qurʾān in the believer's chest and heart, but the niche does not correspond to faith as a matched component.
rows.anchor: لأن المشكاة ليست تقابل الإيمان.

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī calls this an extraordinary description of illumination, likening God's light to the description of a niche.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: أي صفة لنوره لعجيبة الشأن في الإضاءة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān reads an omitted noun: the likeness of God's light is like the light of a niche.
rows.anchor: ويظهر لي أن قوله كمشكاة هو على حذف مضاف أي مثل نوره مثل نور مشكاة

rows.speaker: ابن جبير وسعيد بن عياض والجمهور
rows.claim: The majority, Ibn Jubayr, and Saʿīd b. ʿIyāḍ define the niche as a recess or window that does not pass through.
rows.anchor: وهو قول ابن جبير وسعيد بن عياض والجمهور.

rows.speaker: أبو موسى
rows.claim: Abū Mūsā defines the niche as the iron or lead piece holding the wick inside the glass.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو موسى: المشكاة الحديدة والرصاصة التي تكون فيها الفتيل

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid says the niche is the pillar with the lamp on top, and also the iron hooks on which lamps hang.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: المشكاة العمود الذي يكون المصباح على رأسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lamp is a large lamp.
rows.anchor: فيها مصباح أي سراج ضخم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Apparently, the glass is the container of the lamp, as the verse says the lamp is in glass.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن الزجاجة ظرف للمصباح لقوله المصباح في زجاجة

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī specifies Syrian glass, considering it the clearest, though the verse does not specify a region.
rows.anchor: وقدره الزمخشري في زجاج شامي،

rows.speaker: أبو رجاء ونصر بن عاصم
rows.claim: Abū Rajāʾ and Naṣr b. ʿĀṣim read both occurrences of zujāja with kasra on the zāy.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو رجاء ونصر بن عاصم في زجاجة الزجاجة بكسر الزاي

rows.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة ونصر بن عاصم
rows.claim: Ibn Abī ʿAbla and Naṣr b. ʿĀṣim, in the transmission of Ibn Mujāhid, read both with fatḥa on the zāy.
rows.anchor: وابن أبي عبلة ونصر بن عاصم في رواية ابن مجاهد بفتحها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun refers to the glass, whose clear substance intensifies the light and contains the lamp's radiance.
rows.anchor: كأنها أي كأن الزجاجة لصفاء جوهرها وذاتها وهو أبلغ في الإنارة،

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk identifies the bright planet as Venus and compares the glass's brilliance with the famous bright planets.
rows.anchor: قال الضحاك: هو الزهرة شبه الزجاجة في زهرتها

rows.speaker: نافع وابن عامر وحفص وابن كثير
rows.claim: Most of the seven readers, including Nāfiʿ, Ibn ʿĀmir, Ḥafṣ, and Ibn Kathīr, use ḍamma on dāl and geminate rāʾ and yāʾ; it apparently relates to pearls for whiteness and clarity.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور من السبعة نافع وابن عامر وحفص وابن كثير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The common form apparently relates the planet to a pearl because of its whiteness and clarity; another analysis derives it from hamzated darʾ with hamza replaced and assimilated.
rows.anchor: والظاهر نسبة الكوكب إلى الدر لبياضه وصفائه،

rows.speaker: قتادة وزيد بن علي والضحاك
rows.claim: Qatāda, Zayd b. ʿAlī, and al-Ḍaḥḥāk use the same form with fatḥa on dāl; it is also reported from Naṣr, Abū Rajāʾ, and Ibn al-Musayyab.
rows.anchor: وقرأ قتادة وزيد بن علي والضحاك كذلك إلا أنهما فتحا الدال.

rows.speaker: الزهري
rows.claim: Al-Zuhrī reads the form with kasra on dāl.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الزهري كذلك إلا أنه كسر الدال.

rows.speaker: حمزة
rows.claim: Ḥamza reads the word with hamza, from darʾ meaning to repel: stars repel one another, or the planet's light repels darkness.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة كذلك إلا أنه همز من الدرء بمعنى الدفع،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hamzated form has pattern faʿīl; the commentary notes its rarity and compares murīq, suriyya if derived from joy, mirīkh, and possibly ʿiliyya.
rows.anchor: قيل: ولا يوجد فعيل إلا قولهم مريق للعصفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One derivation makes durrī originally fuʿūl, as in subbūḥ, reduced from a heavy ḍamma to kasra, likewise in surratuhu and darratuhu.
rows.anchor: وقيل: دري ووزنه في الأصل فعول كسبوح

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو والكسائي
rows.claim: Abū ʿAmr and al-Kisāʾī read the form with kasra on dāl, a common noun pattern like sikkin and adjective pattern like sakīr.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو والكسائي كذلك إلا أنه كسر الدال

rows.speaker: قتادة وأبان بن عثمان وابن المسيب وأبو رجاء وعمرو بن فائد والأعمش ونصر بن عاصم
rows.claim: A further transmission from these readers has fatḥa on dāl; Ibn Jinnī calls it rare, with sakīna as the only other remembered example.
rows.anchor: وقرأ قتادة أيضا وأبان بن عثمان وابن المسيب وأبو رجاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The worshippers maintain prayer and give zakāt while fearing what comes at resurrection.
rows.anchor: وإقام الصلاة وإيتاء الزكاة وخوفهم ما يكون في البعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage contrasts believers affected by kinds of guidance with disbelievers who cannot receive it, following the mention of guidance to the light.
rows.anchor: ولذلك جاء مقابل المؤمنين وهم الكفار في قوله والذين كفروا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent sense is the generic plural: houses as a class.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن قوله في بيوت أريد به مدلوله من الجمعية

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan identifies the houses as the Jerusalem sanctuary, called plural because it contains distinct, partitioned spaces.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: أريد به بيت المقدس، وسمي بيوتا من حيث فيه مواضع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account says the Israelites carefully maintained its lamps with specially prepared, sanctified oil sealed in its containers, which made the light brighter.
rows.anchor: ويؤثر أن عادة بني إسرائيل في وقيده في غاية التهمم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The generic wording covers mosques and houses where prayer and learning take place.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن في بيوت مطلق فيصدق على المساجد والبيوت

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid identifies the houses as the homes of the Messenger.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: بيوت الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن ومجاهد
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Ḥasan, and Mujāhid identify them as mosques customarily lit with this type of lamp.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس والحسن أيضا ومجاهد: هي المساجد

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view identifies the houses as the Kaʿba, Jerusalem sanctuary, the Prophet's mosque, and Qubāʾ mosque.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الكعبة وبيت المقدس ومسجد الرسول عليه الصلاة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view identifies them as the houses of the prophets.
rows.anchor: وقيل: بيوت الأنبياء. ويقوي أنها المساجد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mention of glorification in the houses morning and evening strengthens the mosque interpretation.
rows.anchor: ويقوي أنها المساجد قوله يسبح له فيها بالغدو والآصال

rows.speaker: الحسن والضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan and al-Ḍaḥḥāk interpret raising the houses as honoring and exalting them.
rows.anchor: وأمره بأن ترفع أي يعظم قدرها قاله الحسن والضحاك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Mujāhid understand this as building the houses and raising them, as Abraham and Ishmael raised the foundations.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس ومجاهد: تبنى وتعلى من قوله وإذ يرفع إبراهيم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another gloss says the houses are to be purified of filth and sins.
rows.anchor: وقيل: ترفع تطهر من الأنجاس والمعاصي

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another gloss says needs are raised there to God.
rows.anchor: وقيل: ترفع أي ترفع فيها الحوائج إلى الله

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another gloss says voices are raised there in remembrance of God and Qurʾān recitation.
rows.anchor: وقيل: ترفع الأصوات بذكر الله وتلاوة القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording apparently covers every kind of remembrance without restriction.
rows.anchor: ويذكر فيها اسمه ظاهره مطلق الذكر فيعم كل ذكر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains remembrance as God's oneness, namely lā ilāha illā Allāh.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس: توحيده وهو لا إله إلا الله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās also says God's book is recited in the houses.
rows.anchor: وعنه: يتلى فيها كتابه. وقيل: أسماؤه الحسنى.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another gloss takes the phrase to mean God's beautiful names.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أسماؤه الحسنى. وقيل: يصلى

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another gloss takes it to mean that prayer is performed in the houses.
rows.anchor: وقيل: يصلى فيها. وقرأ الجمهور يسبح

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read yusabbiḥu with kasra on bāʾ and yāʾ as its first consonant.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور يسبح بكسر الباء وبالياء من تحت

rows.speaker: ابن وثاب وأبو حيوة
rows.claim: Ibn Waththāb and Abū Ḥaywa use the same vocalization but with tāʾ as the first consonant.
rows.anchor: وابن وثاب وأبو حيوة كذلك إلا أنه بالتاء من فوق

rows.speaker: ابن عامر وأبو بكر والبحتري عن حفص ومحبوب عن أبي عمرو والمهال عن يعقوب والمفضل وأبان
rows.claim: These readers use fatḥa on bāʾ and yāʾ initially; one of the preceding genitives then serves as the passive subject, with the nearer one preferred because the verb selects its subject more strongly.
rows.anchor: وابن عامر وأبو بكر والبحتري عن حفص ومحبوب عن أبي عمرو

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Abū Jaʿfar reads tusabbaḥ with tāʾ initially and fatḥa on bāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر: تسبح بالتاء من فوق وفتح الباء

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī explains the passive reading by treating the morning and evening times as the subject, with an additional bāʾ, so that the times themselves are glorified.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري: ووجهها أن تسند إلى أوقات الغدو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān also allows an implicit verbal noun, tasbīḥa, to serve as the passive subject, as in the passive reading of li-yujzā.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون المفعول الذي لم يسم فاعله ضمير التسبيحة

rows.speaker: أبو مجلز
rows.claim: Abū Mujliz reads al-īṣāl in place of al-āṣāl.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو مجلز: والإيصال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the two passive readings, rijāl may be the agent of an omitted verb, yusabbiḥu or yusabbaḥu lahum; alternatively it is the predicate of an omitted subject, al-musabbiḥ rijāl.
rows.anchor: وارتفع رجال على هاتين القراءتين على الفاعلية بإضمار فعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One syntactic analysis allows a construction like ḍuribat Hind Zayd, while another makes rijāl a predicate of an omitted subject.
rows.anchor: فعلى اقتياسه نحو ضربت هند زيد أي ضربها زيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One possibility is that the men have no trade or sales at all that could distract them, like a road with no beacon to guide travelers.
rows.anchor: أحدهما: أنهم لا تجارة لهم ولا بيع فيلهيهم عن ذكر الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The other possibility is that they do trade and sell but are not distracted from God's remembrance or their obligations.
rows.anchor: والثاني: أنهم ذوو تجارة وبيع ولكن لا يشغلهم ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent coordination distinguishes trade from sale; trade may mean buying paired with sale, or caravan commerce paired with market sales.
rows.anchor: والظاهر مغايرة التجارة والبيع، ولذلك عطف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, sale is a specific kind after the general term trade, which includes buying and selling to seek profit.
rows.anchor: لأن التجارة هي البيع والشراء طلبا للربح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sale is singled out because an imminent profitable deal is more distracting than a hoped-for gain: the former is certain and the latter only expected.
rows.anchor: ونبه على هذا الخاص لأنه في الإلهاء أدخل

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says the tāʾ in iqāma replaces the lost root consonant; the original was iqwām, and annexation removes the compensating tāʾ.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري: التاء في إقامة عوض من العين الساقطة

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ holds that the tāʾ drops because of annexation; the Basrans hold that it does not drop for that reason.
rows.anchor: وهذا الذي ذكر من أن التاء سقطت لأجل الإضافة هو مذهب الفراء

rows.speaker: خالد بن كلثوم
rows.claim: Khālid b. Kulthūm interprets ʿadā al-amr in the cited poem as the plural of ʿidwa, meaning the sides or aspects of a matter.
rows.anchor: وقد تأول خالد بن كلثوم قوله عدا الأمر على أنه جمع عدوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The day they fear is the Day of Resurrection.
rows.anchor: يخافون يوما هو يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hearts and eyes are shaken by the terror of that day, shifting from hope of salvation to hope and from fear of ruin to ruin; the state is like that in 33:10.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن معنى تتقلب تضطرب من هول ذلك اليوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Arabs also use this kind of turning for the turmoil of battle, as in a cited line likening the heart to a bird's wings.
rows.anchor: وهذا المعنى تستعمله العرب في الحروب كقوله:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gloss that hearts turn on Hell's embers is remote because that occurs after the Day of Resurrection, not on it.
rows.anchor: ويبعد قول من قال تتقلب على جمر جهنم لأن ذلك ليس في يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation says hearts and eyes turn from false beliefs to the revealed truth, understanding and seeing after being sealed and blind.
rows.anchor: وقول من قال إن تقلبها ظهور الحق لها أي فتتقلب عن معتقدات الضلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān prefers the first interpretation as more forceful in magnifying the day's terror.
rows.anchor: والقول الأول أبلغ في التهويل.

rows.speaker: ابن محيصن
rows.claim: Ibn Muḥayṣin assimilates the tāʾ in ta-taqallabu into the following tāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن محيصن: تقلب بإدغام التاء في التاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in li-yajziyahum may attach to an omitted verb, or apparently to yusabbiḥu.
rows.anchor: واللام في ليجزيهم متعلقة بمحذوف أي فعلوا ذلك ليجزيهم

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī explains that they glorify God and fear the day so that He may reward them.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: والمعنى يسبحون ويخافون ليجزيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yakhāfūna is an adjective describing rijāl, as lā tulhīhim is.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن قوله يخافون صفة لرجال كما أن لا تلهيهم كذلك.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A deleted noun is understood: the best reward for what they did, or the best recompense for their deeds.
rows.anchor: أحسن هو على حذف مضاف أي ثواب أحسن ما عملوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gives beyond what their deeds warrant; the people of Paradise remain in perpetual increase.
rows.anchor: ويزيدهم من فضله على ما تقتضيه أعمالهم، فأهل الجنة أبدا

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says their reward is doubled and God's additional giving exceeds the reward; al-ḥusnā wa-ziyāda means the best recompense and a further gift.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: ليجزيهم ثوابهم مضاعفا ويزيدهم على الثواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān criticizes al-Zamakhsharī's claim that reward is according to entitlement as a covert Muʿtazilite premise.
rows.anchor: وفي قوله على حسب الاستحقاق دسيسة اعتزال.

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: Most commentators hold that Sūrat al-Furqān is Meccan.
rows.anchor: هذه السورة مكية في قول الجمهور

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Qatāda say three verses, beginning with wa-alladhīna lā yadʿūna and ending wa-kāna Allāhu ghafūran raḥīman, descended at Medina.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس وقتادة: إلا ثلاث آيات نزلت بالمدينة

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says the sura is Medinan except its opening through the phrase wa-lā nushūran, which is Meccan.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك مدنية إلا من أولها إلى قوله ولا نشورا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening answers the previous sura's warning: after obedience, permission, divine dominion, knowledge, and recompense, it begins by declaring God exalted and richly good, including His sending the Furqān as warning.
rows.anchor: ومناسبة أول هذه السورة لآخر ما قبلها أنه لما ذكر وجوب مبايعة المؤمنين للرسول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabāraka is the inchoative form of bāraka, a nonconjugating verb used only of God, without a present, active participle, or verbal noun.
rows.anchor: وتبارك تفاعل مطاوع بارك وهو فعل لا يتصرف ولم يستعمل في غيره تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poem attributed to al-Ṭirmāḥ in the preceding passage says God is blessed: none can give what He withholds, and none can withhold what He gives.
rows.anchor: تباركت لا معط لشيء منعته ... وليس لما أعطيت يا رب مانع

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses tabāraka as He has always existed and will never cease.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: لم يزل ولا يزول

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalīl glosses the word as being majestic or glorified.
rows.anchor: وقال الخليل: تمجد

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk glosses it as being exalted.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك: تعظم

rows.speaker: الأصمعي
rows.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿī reports an Arab saying tabāraka ʿalaykum on reaching a hill, meaning you have ascended or risen; these glosses make it an attribute of essence.
rows.anchor: وحكى الأصمعي تبارك عليكم من قول عربي صعد رابية

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن والنخعي
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Ḥasan, and al-Nakhaʿī derive it from baraka, the increase of good from God, making it an attribute of action.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس أيضا والحسن والنخعي: هو من البركة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the baraka derivation, the meaning is that God's good and gifts increase and multiply.
rows.anchor: فالمعنى زاد خيره وعطاؤه وكثر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the audience denies that God sent down the Furqān, the relative clause is known by proof because the Qurʾān's inimitability establishes it.
rows.anchor: وإن كانوا لا يقرون بأنه تعالى هو الذي نزل الفرقان فقد قام الدليل على إعجازه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān refers back to his discussion in Āl ʿImrān of why the Qurʾān is called the Furqān.
rows.anchor: وتقدم في آل عمران لم سمي القرآن فرقانا

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read the singular, referring to God's servant Muḥammad.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور على عبده وهو الرسول محمد

rows.speaker: ابن الزبير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr reads the plural, referring to the Messenger and his community, supported by language addressing the group.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن الزبير على عباده أي الرسول وأمته كما قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān considers it unlikely that the plural means revealed books and their recipients, with ʿibād used generically as in the phrase niʿmat Allāh.
rows.anchor: ويبعد أن يراد بالقرآن الكتب المنزلة، وبعبده من نزلت عليهم

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says the pronoun in li-yakūna returns to God's servant; Abū Ḥayyān prefers this because the servant is the main subject of the governing verb.
rows.anchor: قال ابن زيد: عائد على عبده ويترجح بأنه العمدة المسند إليه الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nadhīr means mundhir, a warner; it may also be a verbal noun meaning warning, as nakīr means inkār.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن نذيرا بمعنى منذر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verbal-noun reading is supported by the Qurʾānic phrase fa-kayfa kāna ʿadhābī wa-nudhuri.
rows.anchor: ومنه فكيف كان عذابي ونذر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word encompasses humans and jinn, both Muḥammad's contemporaries and later generations, as established by a mass-transmitted report and the apparent verses.
rows.anchor: وللعالمين عام للإنس والجن، ممن عاصره أو جاء بعده

rows.speaker: ابن الزبير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr's reading explicitly glosses the worlds as jinn and humans.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن الزبير للعالمين للجن والإنس وهو تفسير للعالمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The previous sura said that everything in heaven and earth belongs to God; this verse adds that He rules and subdues heaven, earth, and their contents, joining ownership and dominion.
rows.anchor: ولما سبق في أواخر السورة ألا إن لله ما في السموات والأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The relative al-ladhī can be set off for praise in nominative or accusative, or construed as an adjective or appositive of the first al-ladhī; the following clause remains part of its relative clause.
rows.anchor: والذي مقطوع للمدح رفعا أو نصبا
